_comment: Commit this into the project's .claude/settings.json. A member who clones the repo is participating immediately: nothing to install, no credential to create, no command to remember. Paths below assume the two hook scripts are vendored into the repo at hooks/.
_one_source_of_truth: autoMemoryDirectory is the only place the notes' location is written. The hook reads this same key rather than taking a path of its own, because a second copy of the path is a second thing to get wrong — and getting it wrong leaves the pipeline dead with every log line clean. Any path works; it does not need to be called 'memory'.
_over_the_internet: If the host is not on the LAN, this must be https:// and the endpoint must require Basic auth — ingest.js refuses to bind a non-loopback address without TLS in front, because basic auth puts the credential on the wire in a reversible form on every note. Neither value below is a secret and both are committed with the repo; the credential itself lives in .claude/agent-knowledge.env, which each member copies once from hooks/agent-knowledge.env.sample and which is gitignored.
_two_runtimes: Both hooks are registered on purpose and no detection logic is needed. Claude Code never runs on Node — even the npm package only downloads a native binary — so node is not implied on any platform; and a POSIX shell is not implied either, since native Windows without Git for Windows has none. A hook whose runtime is missing fails silently without blocking the other one (measured), and on a machine that can run both, the endpoint's dedupe collapses the duplicate (also measured). hooks/parity-test.js asserts the two send byte-identical notes.

_notes.why_posttooluse: It fires on the write itself. SessionEnd is capped at 1.5s, is killed at teardown, and does not fire on /clear, on a crash, or on Ctrl-C — so anything hung off the end of a session loses notes depending on how the session happened to finish.
_notes.why_http_not_git: Pushing needs a credential that happens to be present and unexpired on that laptop. Both git transports were built and measured and both worked, and both were rejected for exactly that reason.
_notes.cost: The hook adds roughly 160ms to a write inside the memory directory, and about 100ms of node startup to every other Write or Edit, where it exits after one string comparison.
_notes.identity: Attribution comes from the Claude account in ~/.claude.json — accountUuid as the counting key, email as a readable label. That account is always present, because the agent could not have written the note without it, while `git config user.email` is often unset on a fresh machine and is sometimes a shared CI address; git is kept only for the case where the account file cannot be read. Mixing the two sources is the real hazard: one person keyed two ways counts as two people and promotes entries on their own, so the endpoint warns when one label shows up under two keys. A note that cannot be attributed at all is never sent.

_optional_telemetry._why: Not on the critical path — the pipeline runs without any of it. Telemetry answers the one question the notes cannot: did a session run and produce nothing at all, which is the only way to see the CLAUDE.md instruction quietly stopping to work. None of these expose content; OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS is deliberately absent.
